name: _sparse_semi_structured_tile
description: Representative ATen signature, copied verbatim from the supplied registered schema and NOT an exclusive ABI: aten::_sparse_semi_structured_tile(Tensor input, str algorithm="", bool use_cutlass=True) -> (Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor). All supplied registered schema strings (verbatim): aten::_sparse_semi_structured_tile(Tensor input, str algorithm="", bool use_cutlass=True) -> (Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor, Tensor). Only this one overload is registered in the supplied evidence, so there are no further registered signatures to list. The original Gems pytest owns the full contract for this operator: it defines the accepted call forms (omitted algorithm, explicit "", "largest_values_greedy", "largest_abs_values_greedy", together with use_cutlass=True/False where the tile geometry admits them, and with algorithm passed positionally), the five-tensor return, use_cutlass exercised as a keyword, the runtime errors for bad rank, unaligned columns, unsupported layouts, unknown or ill-typed algorithm values, cutlass geometry and, on the vendor where that rejection was measured, rejected dtypes, plus the read-only (non-mutating) input behavior. This definition model must never be narrowed to the representative signature and no test may be removed or its reference behavior adapted to fit it. Semantics derived from the tests: the operator consumes a 2-D dense tile and produces five tensors describing the semi-structured sparsification of that tile (packed values/metadata decomposition); native execution was measured reproducible only for 64-aligned rows and columns (128-aligned for the use_cutlass=False path), the dtypes reaching the native kernel are fp16 and, where the static device capability flag allows it, bf16, and the input is only read, never mutated. Conditional, argument-dependent acceptance and error behavior stays in the pytest and is not expressed here.
